counterfactual_rationale: The record says the naive all2all path ran shared experts on dispatched rather than original hidden states and drove DeepSeek-R1 accuracy to zero. A backend/reference MoE test with distinct dispatched and original hidden states would plausibly expose that mismatch before merge.

The CPU communicator assumed torch.distributed all_reduce returned the reduced tensor, and the discussion says the fix unblocked CPU tests. Running the same collective path in CPU CI would plausibly have caught the wrong return-value integration.

The ROCm AITER fused-MoE path asserted out for Llama4 BF16 when apply_router_weight_on_input was true. A ROCm/AITER model-initialization or accuracy job for that model family would plausibly have failed before merge.

The GDN builder classified stateless one-token first chunks as decode, causing reads of stale recurrent/conv state from recycled pages. A serving-style regression that reuses state pages and sends first-token chunks would plausibly reveal the corruption.

The XPU encoder-decoder KV path used token-granular page tables and a decoder region that could start mid-page, producing garbage for page_size > 1. A reference test varying encoder length and page size, especially non-page-aligned lengths such as 1500, would plausibly catch it.

The TileLang mHC kernel carried a cross-row reduction accumulator between rows for block-M cases such as num_tokens=2048. Kernel-vs-reference tests that include the block-M token range would plausibly expose the odd-row corruption.

The FlashInfer backend skipped save_kv_cache although DLLM later needs to attend to the cache, and the linked issue cites a failing LLaDA2 test. A DLLM execution test through that backend would plausibly catch the missing cache write.
The XPU MRoPE path could pass a float32 cos/sin cache with bfloat16 Q/K and trigger a dtype RuntimeError. XPU CI covering multimodal RoPE with bf16 inputs would plausibly have exposed the mismatch.

The FP8 MoE path omitted the model-provided SwiGLU clamp, causing garbled DeepSeek-V4 Base outputs and low eval quality. Tests using realistic activations or clamp-sensitive values would plausibly reveal the missing clamp better than generic small random inputs.

The transformers backend crashed in the fused allreduce+rms_norm path because the fused code unpacked a tensor shape with too many dimensions. A TP transformers-backend generation smoke test would plausibly trigger the same fused-op shape mismatch.

Both FlashInfer and Triton attention assumed a uniform head count, corrupting outputs or writing out of bounds for per-layer head-count models. Reference tests varying num_attention_heads_per_layer would plausibly expose the bad planning and sizing.

The record says a CPU replacement for a Triton slot-mapping kernel was added and CPU CI softfail was removed, but it does not show a concrete failing behavior or root cause. I could not confidently determine whether this is a kernel-correctness fix rather than support/CI enablement.

Hopper defaults to FA3, which does not support ALiBi and made ALiBi models fail to start until the backend fell back to FA2. Running ALiBi model coverage on Hopper/FA3 would plausibly have caught the unsupported backend selection.

The HiCache JIT kernel failed to compile with the recorded tvm-ffi dependency error. CI that actually builds the JIT kernel under the affected dependency/compiler combination would plausibly have caught the failure.

The FA3 AOT scheduler path on H100 mishandled sliding-window attention and produced incorrect results. H100 CI running sliding-window correctness tests against a reference would plausibly have exposed the regression.

The W4AFP8 MoE kernel occasionally produced incorrect and same-seed inconsistent results, especially with larger batches and many experts. Repeated kernel/reference runs with varied batch and expert counts would plausibly expose the nondeterministic failure.

The FlashInfer-backed path failed with 'too many resources requested for launch' until the dependency version was updated. A matrix job that launches the affected backend with the old FlashInfer/kernel combination would plausibly catch it.

The record only says old Triton MoE configs were copied to fix a CI regression and links a failed job, without a visible correctness symptom or root-cause detail. I could not confidently assign a kernel failure class from the excerpt.

The TRT-LLM MXFP4 fake op returned a padded shape while the real kernel wrote the unpadded width, causing torch.compile assertions on Blackwell TP runs. Blackwell compile/serve CI for the affected gpt-oss MXFP4 path would plausibly catch the fake/real mismatch.

On ROCm AITER, preshuffled MXFP4 weights were dispatched as unshuffled, producing nonsense and a large GSM8K drop. ROCm AITER accuracy coverage with the GPT-OSS MXFP4 weight layout would plausibly expose the wrong codegen branch.

The record states that moving AOT kernels to JIT broke the MUSA sglang-kernel build and the fix was validated by setup_musa.py install. MUSA build CI for the kernel package would plausibly have caught the failure.

The PR fixed a decode throughput regression and MTP acceptance-rate regression by restoring kernel selection for a Blackwell GLM GPTQ configuration. A model-level performance/acceptance benchmark on that hardware and quantization mix would plausibly detect it.

The gpu_only spec_v2 path crashed when None metadata and missing CPU lengths reached Triton attention consumers. A speculative-decoding server test on the gpu_only path would plausibly exercise the same initialization and metadata assumptions.

The ROCm AITER fake custom op signature omitted arguments accepted by the real op, crashing FakeTensor/torch.compile for the MXFP4 CK path. ROCm compile coverage of that AITER MoE path would plausibly have triggered the TypeError.

A large fused_moe run hit a GPU SEGV at tl.load, and the fix widened offsets to int64 to avoid integer overflow. A memcheck-style run or large-shape reference test would plausibly flag the illegal access before merge.

The FlashInfer min_p sampler API did not return success states as the SGLang sampler expected, producing crashes. A sampling-path test that exercises min_p through the FlashInfer backend would plausibly catch the interface mismatch.

The Triton fused MoE LoRA kernel wrote LoRA additions to the wrong rows of intermediate_cache1, producing bad gpt-oss LoRA outputs. A fused-kernel-vs-reference LoRA test with row reordering would plausibly expose the mis-indexing.

The NVFP4 EP path left some input-scale rows uninitialized when the logical-to-physical expert map skipped physical rows, causing NaN scaling. Tests with sparse physical-expert mappings would plausibly reveal the undefined scale reads.

The fused Kimi-K3 front GEMM computed router logits in bf16 although the router needed fp32, changing top-k expert sets and hurting accuracy. Model-weight or adversarial-value tests around router decision boundaries would plausibly expose the precision loss.

NemotronH on XPU failed first on a missing device guard and then on Triton backend layer indexing for hybrid Mamba2/full-attention layouts. XPU initialization tests for hybrid Mamba2 models would plausibly catch both launch blockers.
